column1: I judge others harshly, and myself even more severely.
I put too much trust in those who wield power within my temple’s hierarchy.
My piety sometimes leads me to blindly trust those that profess faith in my god.
I am inflexible in my thinking.
I am suspicious of strangers and expect the worst of them.
Once I pick a goal, I become obsessed with it to the detriment of everything else in my life.
I speak to my horse in a sickly sweet, sing-song manner.
I’ve been known to fly into a rage like a wild boar when I am angered.
I have no table manners whatsoever. I tear my food with my teeth and fingers, eschewing silverware altogether.

I refuse to eat animals of any kind and am always trying to convert my traveling companions to vegetarians. 5 When I see someone mistreating their mount, I’m likely to deliver them a beating they’ll never forget. (I’ve landed in lock up once or twice because of this.)
I can’t say no to a stray animal. I’ll give it my last scrap of food (and yours too, if I can get away with it).
I am incredibly jealous of those with more knowledge than me.
I’m lazy, an honest day’s work is a great punishment to me.
I am a coward, what good is loot if you’re dead?
I am incredibly greedy, I will attempt to take all the best spoils, even if it means lying to my comrades.
My drive for antiques causes me to disregard the danger of my choices.
I refuse to admit being wrong, even when I know the other party is right.
I am easily moved to violence.
I’ll put myself and others in danger if it earns me some coin.
The only way to live with what I’ve done is to wallow in alcohol and the pleasures of the flesh.
I often succumb to the “better part of valor,” and run away.
I don’t pay attention to finer details. Just point me in a direction and I’ll hack it up.
People who know me best don’t trust me because I’m always just out for myself.
Even when in service, I worked poorly with others. I find it hard to make connections.
I am stubborn to a dangerous fault.
I lie even when there is no need to do so.
My belief in the Empire often causes me to get into fights when I hear others insulting it.
I am bad with directions and often get lost.
I am absent-minded and will sometimes forget to do regular tasks.
I get everything I touch sticky.
I‘m a picky eater. I only eat sweet things.
I keep up an incessant humming which drives people nuts.
I put on a big show of bravado, but I’m all bark and no bite.
I downplay danger, sometimes rushing headlong into a perilous situation.
My attention wanders. I flit from one thought or activity to the next without pause.
I have trouble keeping my mouth shut.
I am dimwitted and need to have instructions repeated to me.
I am a social outcast and do not do well with other people.
I am noticeably ugly with an easy to remember face.
I hate working with teams.
I lack resolve.
I am clumsy and often trip up at the worst times.
I am dedicated to physical training at the expense of all else, I can barely read.
I get nervous in front of large crowds.
I am willing to cheat to win.
I train even when my body is injured.
I wish pain on those who show me up.
I’m actually a bit of a prude.
I complain if I have to walk long distances.
I talk too much.
I like to steal from my clients.
Seeing someone prettier than me drives me into a rage.
I always want to be the center of attention.
I would rather serve darkness than serve no one.
I’m afraid of taking risks that might be good for me.
I believe my master’s people are superior to all others, and I’m not afraid to share that truth.
I always do as I’m told, even though sometimes I don’t think I should.
I know what’s best for everyone, and they’d all be better off if they’d follow my advice.
I can’t stand seeing ugly or depressing things. I’d much rather think happy thoughts
I have little concern for the problems of others.
I will keep an eye on your valuables and help myself to them if I get the chance.
Generosity will only deprive me of that which I need to survive. Better to let them perish than waste my resources.
I am quick to anger, and I don’t care if I hurt your feelings.
I am opportunistic and will exploit your weaknesses in order to get ahead.
I distrust magic and those who practice the forbidden arts.
I enjoy the company of camels more than people.
I can be loud and boorish after a few wineskins.
If I feel insulted, I’ll refuse to speak to anyone for several hours.
I enjoy violence and mayhem a bit too much.
You can’t rely on me in a crisis.
I betrayed my brother to cultists to save my own skin.
If you don’t have a destiny, are you really special?
But I am the “Chosen One.”
I fear commitment; that’s what this boils down to in the end.
What if I follow through with this and I fail?
It doesn’t matter what someone else sacrificed for this. I only care about my feelings.
Occasionally—ok, maybe “often”—I make poor decisions in life, like running from this destiny.
I always start by appealing to a better nature from those I face, regardless of their apparent hostility.
I assume the best in everyone, even if I have been betrayed by that trust in the past.
I will stand in the way of an ally to ensure conflicts don’t start.
I believe I can always talk my way out of a problem.
I chastise those who are rude or use vulgar language.
When I feel I am on the verge of a successful negotiation, I often push my luck to obtain further concessions.
I refuse to wear clothes that are not black or gray; I’d rather die of cold.
I am pessimistic and nihilistic, and I often give up hope too soon.
I hear veiled insults and sarcasm even in the harmless words of those who did not intend to offend me.
I am terribly jealous and possessive of anyone close to me.
I am unpredictable and I switch between moments of apathy and explosions of anger and violence, and then sink into desperate weeping.
I hide dark thoughts that I have not been able to get out of my head.
I have a bad sense of direction.
I am not sociable and wish to be left to my own devices.
I am a coward; the desert makes a good hiding place.
I am greedy and will readily leave someone behind if they cannot pay.
I hate the heat.
I distrust those from outside the dunes.
I refuse to provide healing unless I am compensated.
I nag others to give up habits I deem to be unhealthy.
I become indignant if someone questions my healing methods.
I hover like a mother hen when anyone I care about gets injured.
I am always handing out health advice, even when it’s unsolicited.
Having treated so many serious injuries, I have no compassion for those who whine over nothing.
I betrayed a fellow slave in order to escape. I *don’t* regret it.
I am easily angered by insults and slights. My owner pursues me relentlessly. They want me back,
Dead or alive.
I assume that anyone who is overly friendly is trying to trick me.
I go out of my way to flout authority.
I can’t limit myself when it comes to alcohol or other substances.
My competitive nature causes conflict with friends
If I have to choose between my friends and my athletic career, I will choose my career
I like the spotlight and am not a team player
I have a weakness that sabotages me during major sporting events
I aggressively confront all potential challengers
I won an event due to an unfair advantage, and I’m ok with that.
I wish to punish those responsible for my exile.
I resent all of civilization.
Now that I am exiled, I can do whatever I want.
They should have exiled me long ago; I’ve done so many bad things.
My testimony would have exonerated an innocent man, but I remained silent and he got exiled too.
I am suspicious of everyone, especially those who seek me out.
I distrust people who don’t do honest labor.
I do things my way or I don’t do them at all.
I have what I need to survive, I don’t need anyone else.
I am quick to assume someone is trying to take advantage of me.
I am superstitious for good reason. My predictions are almost always right!
I would kill to expand my farm into an estate.
I am accustomed to doing what I like when I like. I’m bad at compromising, and I must exert real effort to make even basic conversation with other people.
I won’t harm a beast without just cause or provocation.
Years of isolated living has left me blind to the nuances of social interaction. It is a struggle not to view every new encounter through the lens of fight or flight.
The decay after death is merely the loam from which new growth springs—and I enjoy nurturing new growth.
An accident that I caused incurred great damage upon my forest, and, as penance, I have placed myself in self-imposed exile.
I distrust the undead and the unliving, and I refuse to work with them.
It’s all about me! Haven’t you learned that by now?
I can identify every weapon and item with a look.
You think this is bad? Let me tell you about something really frightening.
Sure, I have old foes around every corner, but who doesn’t?
I’m getting too old for this.
Seeing the bad side in everything just protects you from inevitable disappointment.
I’m terrified by the desert. Not enough water, far too much sand.
I drink too much and end up starting barroom brawls.
I killed one of my shipmates and took his share of the loot.
I take unnecessary risks and often put my friends in danger.
I sold captives taken at sea to traders.
Most of the time, I find it impossible to tell the truth.
Individuals can be all right, but civilization is the worst.
The wealthy and nobility are a rot in society.
Things die, either by predators or nature; get used to it.
Everything can be managed if you want it badly enough.
When you make exceptions, you allow unworthy or wasteful things to survive.
If you don’t work hard for something, is it worth anything?
I have an unhealthy obsession for items of buried antiquity.
I secretly harbor dark thoughts and strange scientific or eldritch ambitions
A life of isolation has led me to be brooding and uncommunicative, despite frequently thinking aloud and mumbling to myself.
My fascination with the dead and the afterlife goes well beyond some peoples’ sense of what is considered healthy.
I am obsessed with my quest for personal immortality.
Years of social detachment and seclusion have made me over-analytical, eccentric, and suspicious.
My fingernails are always caked with dirt.
I’m constantly picking at my teeth with a sliver of wood.
I only buy flawless produce- if it’s not perfect, I don’t want it.
The knees of my pants are torn and stained. I can’t keep any clothes nice.
I badmouth anyone I know involved with wanton destruction of forested areas.
I’ve used my knowledge of harmful plants to keep my rival in the latrine all day, and I didn’t feel an ounce of remorse!
I am hot-headed and quick to anger.
I am lazy and slow to rouse.
I am a coward and keep to the safety of the trees.
I am resentful to the towns and cities for the toll they take on nature.
I often misunderstand social situations.
I am slow to trust outsiders.
I’m still very, very evil.
Even when I try to do good, my sinister appearance and mannerisms make me hard to trust.
I’ve held my true past a secret and I will do anything to keep it that way.
A little murder never hurt anybody.
I am intensely jealous of heroes more popular than me.
I refuse to give others a second chance, despite my own background.
I smell of horses, dirt, and smoke.
I promise only that I will make your death swift.
I do not value the lives of people who defile themselves by living in cities.
I have no need for social graces. It is your problem if I offend you.
We see a dog. You see a valued pet and companion. I see dinner.
I am not so optimistic as to think we will live long lives.
People dislike the smell of me.
I am quick to anger, and I need little encouragement to fight.
People who group together in the filth of cities disgust me.
If you care not for my words, you’ll care less for my blade.
Give me roasted meat on the bone and I care not what you think of my decorum.
I steal from the wealthy, but I don’t bother being stealthy about it.
I openly disdain people who do not hunt.
I don’t care about balance or nature, I care about profit.
Poaching adds another layer of excitement to the hunt.
I hate eating farm raised meat.
My skills make me independent and put me in control of most situations. I do what I want and ignore advice.
I jealously guard my hunting ranges.
Even when in service, I worked poorly with others. I find it hard to make connections.
I am stubborn to a dangerous fault.
I lie even when there is no need to do so.
My belief in the Empire often causes me to get into fights when I hear others cheering its fall.
I am bad with directions and often get lost.
I am absent-minded and will sometimes forget to do regular tasks.
I can’t help teasing or criticizing those less intelligent than I.
I love rich food and drink, and I never miss a chance at a good meal.
I never trust anyone who won’t drink with me.
I hate it when people start fights in bars; they never consider the consequences.
I can’t stand to see someone go hungry or sleep in the cold if I can help it.
I am quick to anger if anyone doesn’t like my meals or brews. If you don’t like it, do it yourself.
I’ve done more than my share of humanoid experimentation and I plan to do far more.
I’m the smartest person in the room but I don’t understand why people take offense to me saying that.
You’re wrong, I’m right. End of discussion.
I’ve left behind everything I cared for so many times, I don’t know if I can be connected to anything anymore.
My plans always seem to be ruined by someone who is clearly inferior to me. It enrages me.
I have no respect for any type of law. Mortal, religious, moral, ritual, physical, or intangible.
The pleasures of the flesh are too great for me to resist.
I get a rush from watching someone else die. Sometimes I can’t stop myself.
I am very good with one weapon but cannot seem to master any other.
A chance encounter with true evil has made me fear my own death more than anything else.
I believe I am the chosen one. One day all will wonder at my glory.
I believe that every good thing that happens in this world is solely due to my actions.
I have no respect for those who never signed on to a mercenary company or walked the battlefield.
I cannot bear losing anyone close to me, so I keep everyone at a distance.
Bloody violence is the only way to solve problems.
I caused the downfall of my family’s mercenary company.
I am hiding a horrible secret about one of my family’s patrons.
I see insults to my honor or reputation in every whisper, veiled glance, and knowing look.
I do not trust easily and question anyone who attempts to give me orders.
I ridicule others to hide my insecurities.
To seem brave and competent, I refuse to allow anyone to doubt my courage.
I survived an attack by a monster as a child, and I have feared that creature ever since.
I have a hard time thinking before I act.
I hide my laziness by tricking others into doing my work for me
Lots of monsters die when I research them. More than a normal adventuring party kill.
I’ve made up half of the findings in my research.
I’ve hired a lot of bodyguards for my work. Unless you survive a week or more, I’m not going to bother remembering your name.
My research is more important than my own life or the lives of those around me.
I tend to squander whatever gold my research may bring in.
I’m not above torturing a creature to learn more about them.
What? I like my meat raw. Is that so strange?
I like to collect trophies from my defeated foes (ears, teeth, bones, or similar). It’s how I keep score.
I usually forget about pesky social conventions like “personal property” or “laws.”
I am easily startled by loud noises or bright lights.
I have trouble respecting anyone who can’t best me in a fight.
Kindness is for the weak.
I am jealous of those who have memories of a happy childhood.
I’m desperate for knowledge about my past, and I’ll do anything to obtain that information.
I’m terrified of meeting someone from my past, so I avoid strangers as much as possible.
Only the present matters. I can’t bring myself to care about the future.
I’m convinced that I was powerful and rich before I lost my memories—and I expect everyone to treat me accordingly.
Anyone who shows me pity is subjected to my biting scorn.
I would do anything to forget.
Unnatural monsters blind me with rage or fear.
I regret leaving someone I cared about behind, and rebuff potential friends or allies for fear I might have to abandon them too.
I obsessively stockpile so many things I can’t easily store or track them all, just in case I might need them.
After being failed by those responsible for my safety before, I reflexively question and distrust all authority figures.
I will make any sacrifice to avert or stop even the possibility of a threat like the one that I so narrowly survived.
Only a coward retreats. The valiant press forward to victory or death.
All the tales I tell of my experiences are lies.
Critics and hecklers will suffer my wrath once the performance is over.
Companions and friends cease to be valuable if their accomplishments outshine my own.
I once burned down a tavern where I was poorly received. I would do it again.
I cannot bear to be contradicted and pout when I am.
When stressed, I mutter theories to myself, sometimes connecting seemingly unconnected or random events, to explain my current predicament.
It’s not paranoia if they really are out to get me.
I have a habit of lying to hide my theories and discoveries.
I see secrets and mysteries in everything and everyone.
The world is full of dark secrets, and I’m the only one who can safely unearth them.
There is no law or social convention I won’t break to further my goals.
I can’t resist games of chance.
I cannot pass a tavern without stopping for a few drinks.
I trust people too easily, and it has led to more than a few big mistakes.
Betray my trust and I won’t stop hunting you until I’ve evened the score.
Put a bounty before me and I will eat until there is nothing left.
I wish to own everything I set my eyes upon.
I am a perfectionist and will not perform unless I am sure it will be perfect.
My patrons offer me bountiful food and a little too much drink.
I enraged a previous patron who still has a bounty on my head.
I must always see the story to its end, retreating is difficult for me.
I have grown to despise entertaining others and lament having no other means of survival.
It takes a long time for me to begin trusting my allies.
I am driven to reclaim the status and respect of the socially and scientifically elite and will sacrifice much to gain it.
I am highly competitive and not above plagiarizing or stealing the occasional recipe, idea, formula, or sample.
I am hard-pressed to treat anyone who is not (by my standards) “well schooled” or “well heeled” as little more than lab assistants and house servants.
A pretty face is always able to lead me astray.
I am secretly addicted to a special perfume that only I can reproduce.

On a stormy night, I heard a voice in the wind, which led me to a mysterious plant. Its scent was intoxicating, and I consumed it. Now, that voice occasionally whispers in my dreams, urging me to some unknown destiny
I have an annoying voice.
I am quick to anger, especially towards the lower class.
I am a coward; I rarely leave the walls of my manse.
I am overly gregarious and often don’t know when to shut up.
My greed often clouds my judgement.
I am overly generous and it often threatens my finances.
I have no sense of the importance of property and do not respect others’ property.
I do not take advice—no one has had the experiences I have.
I am prone to overindulge on new intoxicants.
My first instinct when things go bad is to run.
I quickly condemn others for what I perceive are close-minded views.
I’ll do anything just for the chance to see something new.
Every time I think of my previous life, I become enraged at the visions I see.
I believe I am always being watched and am suspicious of everyone.
If no one else is real then only my life is sacred.
I suffer from phantom pains that strike at random.
I think I am the coolest being in existence and will fight anyone who says otherwise.
My memories of this life and my previous life are fading fast. I can barely remember the last year.
I have poor penmanship.
I am slow to recognize sarcasm.
I try to see the best in everyone, even those who truly don’t deserve it.
I care too much what people say about my plays.
I can’t write or read and must dictate my plays.
I can’t stand watching my own performances on stage.
I brag about how much I can lift.
I spend a ridiculous amount of time organizing my gear every morning.
I know the best route to take when traveling. Period. End of discussion.
I’m oblivious to the difficulty others have doing things that come easily to me.
Just because I can carry something, doesn’t mean I should…carry your own stuff!
I do 125 push ups every morning just before my companions rise, calling out each number shrilly as I go. I can’t figure out why my mates don’t appreciate me making sure they wake on time every day.
I feel like a fraud. My work is terrible, and everyone is just too polite to tell me otherwise.
I have a lot of trouble starting anything. I plan, research, and plan some more, but I just can’t seem to start.
What do you mean you don’t know my name!?
I steal the work, plans, or ideas of others and pass it off as my own.
I have dark and terrible dreams every night. I work to forget them.
I hate seeing others succeed.
I’ll do anything to get a major contract with a wealthy client.
I am suspicious of most other people.
No one can ever know that I cheated on my final exams.
My ambition causes me to take on questionable clients.
I would kill to turn this job into an aristocratic title.
I can’t stand it when someone else might be as good at my profession as I am.
I will forever hide my past.
I am no more trustworthy than I can trust others.
I don’t regret my past.
Given the right circumstances, I’d go back to banditry.
I sometimes have nightmares over what I’ve done. I don’t know if I can escape my guilt.
I have a nervous tick that’s easy to tell once you look for it. I hope I don’t give myself away.
I believe my reawakened status makes me better than other people.
Having known other lives, I am obsessed with squeezing every drop of experience out of this one.
Feeling certain I will always return again, I am sometimes foolhardy and heedless of risk.
I am often obsessed with my past lives to the point of neglecting my present one.
I am certain that my present life is some sort of punishment visited upon me.
I tend to trust things and people I feel a past-life connection to a little too much.
My plans often take a deadly turn because I don’t plan properly.
I misinterpret cosmic signal every time I receive them.
All lives are without true value, all that matters is our dogma.
I am cowardly and run at the first sign of trouble.
Being unique is the most important thing in the world to me.
I have a pit of anger in my stomach that no amount of revenge will fill, but I still try anyway.
Enemies from my homeland still pursue me even here.
I’m overly fatalistic, always expecting the worst from circumstances and, often, from people.
Proud and determined, I have a difficult time accepting help.
Times of deprivation have made me stingy when it comes to spending money or resources.
I tend to assume responsibility for everything, even things that are not my fault.
I have a difficult time establishing close relationships and putting down roots because I assume nothing is going to last.
I am quick to anger.
Despite my station, I feel fear when going into battle.
I don’t think I could commit ritual suicide if I violate my bushido code.
My body odor is powerful, and it becomes even more so in my armor.
I crack jokes often and am frequently told they are not funny.
I am quick to judge the characters of other people, and I have been wrong about them before.
If there’s a lever to pull, I’ll pull it.
It’s not stealing if nobody realizes it’s gone.
If I don’t like the odds, I’m out of there.
I often don’t know when to shut up.
I once filched a pipe from a priest. Now I think the god has cursed me.
I grow angry when someone else steals the limelight
I smell of old leather and sea salt.
I spend my coin faster than I earn it.
I have taken jobs repairing ships for people I don’t like, and left weaknesses in their ship’s hulls.
I think some dogs are more worth saving than their owners.
I have a price on my head.
I often act before thinking things through.
I speak my mind too often before those I shouldn’t.
I am illiterate.
I am too timid and rarely assert myself.
I have an addiction to gambling.
I get sea sick.
I boast about my history even where and when I shouldn’t.
Paranoia consumes my every waking moment. Every shadow is another enemy.
I’ve built up a web so complex that I believe no one will ever bring me down.
People are just tools to me, there to be used.
I just have to know everything.
I am smarter than everyone else, actually.
I can’t. Stop. Lying.
I have a callous disposition which many find off-putting.
My obsession with the afterlife grows by the day. I find the world in which I currently reside dull by comparison.
I have no fear of death. A complete lack of self-preservation has nearly cost me my life on more than one occasion.
I deeply distrust adherents of other religions, and even worshipers of Egyptian gods different from my own.
My greed has been known to get the best of me. I sometimes steal offerings intended for the deceased.
I am deeply lonely. Sometimes I feel as if only the dead truly understand me.
Sometimes I may overindulge in a guilty pleasure, but you need something to pass time.
I can’t just sit quietly next to someone. I’ve got to fill the silence with conversation to make good company.
I’m not very capable in social situations. I’d rather sit on the sidelines and observe. People make me nervous.
I have a tough time trusting strangers and new people. You don’t know their habits and behaviors; therefore, you don’t know their risk.
There is danger all around us, and only the foolish let their guard down. I am no fool, and I will spot the danger.
I believe there’s a firm separation between task and personal time. I don’t do other people’s work when I’m on my own time. If you want me, hire me
Knowing the dangers that exist, I am mistrustful almost to the point of paranoia.
I feel the need to drown my unpleasant memories in revelry, good times, and strong drink.
Shadow haunts me, always, in my nightmares and in my worst imaginings and temptations.
I am sometimes unsympathetic, seeing suffering as weakness. After all, I survived, didn’t I? So will you.
Deep down, I feel that I am forever corrupt and tainted because of what happened to me.
I am driven relentlessly by my Bond, often to the exclusion of all else.
I am unnecessarily violent.
I have an unnatural fear of chains and cages.
Nobody can break the hard shell I’ve raised up around my past.
I’m prone to lash out at shows of authority.
I get extremely nervous in busy cities.
I fear wide open spaces.
I am an obsessive haggler; from coppers for the shoeshine boy, to the uncut emeralds for the latest harbormaster’s bribe, I never settle for first price.
I always take a cut, skimming a small percentage off the top of almost anything I handle.
Some think me paranoid because of my hyper-acute awareness and sense for spies, eaves-droppers, and imposters, magical or otherwise
I’ll go a long way to win the favor of the local beauties and fine-featured folk.
My loyalties go to the highest bidder or most lucrative contract, regardless of personal feelings or desires.
I mentally figure out the net worth of people in terms of liquid assets.
I look around and all I see is death and dying.
I don’t think about those whose lives I ended. There’s nothing to gain from that.
I am seriously considering putting a knife through my commander’s skull.
I have left an ally vulnerable in battle because I did not like him.
When met with resistance, I find it easier to fall back than it is to deal with the possibility of being killed.
I have no tolerance for those who fail to keep their bodies in peak condition.
While I was trained in it, I have never been much good at calligraphy, my writing is nearly illegible.
I hate reading, yet there always seems to be another scroll that needs copying!
I am a coward; I prefer to remain safely in the libraries where I belong.
I am quite greedy and have been known to take from the donation crates before they are counted.
I will seek knowledge even at great expense to my health and pocketbook.
I grow resentful of those who seem to know more than me.
I believe earlier people were superior. I constantly complain about modern values.
I let everyone know that I was part of every significant historical event, somehow.
I become enraged when anyone questions my version of history.
I judge other races harshly based on my time’s perception of them.
I will not make friends. They can be lost in an instant.
I take a very long time when I search or study historical sites.
I talk nonstop.
I’m constantly finishing other people’s sentences.
I am always correcting other people’s pronunciation of words.
I can swear in no less than four different languages…and I often do.
I frequently start my sentences with “Didn’t you mean to say…” It drives my companions nuts.
When I’m explaining a new concept to someone, I speak at a painfully slow rate.
I am very dour and rarely see the good in a situation.
I cannot read.
I am averse to violence, why fight when you can speak?
I am greedy and charge heavily for my talents.
I hate people, but I am good at speaking to them.
I get nervous in front of large crowds.
I’m actually a sham. All of my trophies were bagged by someone else. I just followed along and watched.
I’m terrified of anything larger than myself.
I can’t express anger without lashing out at something.
I need money. I don’t care how much or how little I have; I need more. And I would do anything to get it.
I am obsessed with beauty in animals, art, and people.
I don’t trust my hunting partners, whom I know are here to steal my glory!
I care more for a glorious death than I do for any of my subordinates.
I am easily swayed by groveling and displays of submission.
I once made a mistake that crippled my leader’s plan, and will do anything to avoid being found out.
Those who question my plans simply cannot comprehend my genius.
Every time I arrest someone, I get a rush of power.
I have an addiction, and use my authority to feed it.
Cross me and I will think of nothing else until you are dead by my sword.
I don’t care for most people and I’ll only help if there’s something in it for me.
Keep what belongs to you, but don’t even think of taking what’s mine.
If I’m not at sea, I have no cares in the world.
You are lucky to know one such as me.
If you have something I want, I will find a way to make it mine.
I don’t realize when I’m not wanted.
I rarely know where my next coin will come from.
I go so long without proper meals that I often overeat to the point of sickness when food is in abundance.
I have a bad temper and have made enemies in many towns I’ve visited.
I sometimes slip into the wrong language mid conversation, often to great offense.
My wanderlust precludes me from making strong connections.
